editions.title: The edging tape order
editions.independentTeachingDecision: A corner cut removes two boundary segments, a side notch removes one, and an interior hole removes none. Every drawing removes a congruent 3 cm × 2 cm piece.

assignments.bridge: The same offcut comes from a corner, an edge or the centre. Which old edges disappear in each drawing, and which new edges need tape?
assignments.examplePrediction: Trace the outside with your finger. Where did the two touching edges go?

editions.title: The museum ticket machine
editions.independentTeachingDecision: One stamp has a two-valued inverse. A whole-ticket range is filtered by divisibility before reconstruction and checked forwards.

assignments.bridge: Undo the final stamp first. After subtracting two from the smudged range, which tickets could really have come out of the tripling stamp?
assignments.examplePrediction: Which operation happened closest to the answer 17?

assignments.bridge: The distance stamp reads four. Which two tickets could print it, and which one survives the drawer’s admission rule? Carry both candidates into the later puzzle until you can test its input restriction.

editions.title: The climbing hall counter
editions.independentTeachingDecision: The largest numerical rise has the slowest average rate in the arrival log. The price lines cross between whole visits, so the cheaper option changes without an attainable tie.

assignments.bridge: Compare the arrivals using each interval’s own minutes. On the cost chart, can the crossing itself be a legal number of visits?
assignments.examplePrediction: Does the rate depend on the meter's final reading or on how far the reading moved?

assignments.bridge: The longest interval adds twenty-four visitors, while the first interval adds twelve. How many minutes did each rise take, and which has the greater average rate?
